note: Reviewed mappings; highest precedence in the gap report. MAPPED_VERIFIED_LIVE entries were exercised by examples/dart-owner-customers against a running Capitalix backend built from the published source revision, and every recorded exchange was validated against the pinned contract (see docs/ACCEPTANCE_EVIDENCE.md). Only claims that were observed are recorded.

notes: No plain `GET customers` list exists; the paginated customer list is customer-balances.
Response is `data: {items: [...], meta: {current_page, last_page, total}}` (observed live).
Supported filters: name, mobile, payment_status, has_debt, page, per_page (1..100). The app's `search`, `status` and `type` filters are not in the contract.

Rows are balances (customer_reference, name, mobile|null, invoice_count, paid_amount, remaining_amount, payment_status|null, has_debt, has_overdue), not the app's customer object; amounts are decimal strings, not numbers.
Contract field names: mobile (app: phone), tax_number (app: vat_number), commercial_registration_no (app: commercial_register); no is_active on create.
The backend rejected an ORGANIZATION without tax_number (422, observed live); the contract marks tax_number optional — a conditional rule the contract does not express.
409 = likely duplicate; resend with confirm_distinct=true to proceed.
Response `type`/`status` are plain strings in the contract (observed: ORGANIZATION, ACTIVE).
The backend conformance bindings send the app's field names (phone, vat_number, …); whether those are accepted is undocumented and was NOT verified here.
Method is PUT (the app spec suggested POST). Full update: same fields and rules as create.
Not exercised live. The contract's 200 `data` documents only `financial_summary` and `invoices` arrays with untyped items; the customer fields the app expects cannot be determined from the contract.
